stem: Which cellular mechanism is responsible for the arrhythmias seen in CPVT?

options.text: Abnormal calcium handling within myocardial cells.
A total lack of potassium channels in the ventricles.
The physical tearing of the atrial myocardium.
Delayed closure of the mitral valve.

explanation: Excessive calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum makes cells hyperexcitable during stress or exercise.
rationale: Identify the specific mineral involved in cardiac cell excitability.

optionExplanations.A: Excessive calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum makes cells hyperexcitable during stress or exercise.
optionExplanations.B: A complete lack of channels would be incompatible with life; CPVT is specifically a calcium regulation issue.
optionExplanations.C: CPVT is an electrical/calcium handling disorder, not a structural injury or tear.
optionExplanations.D: Mechanical valve issues are distinct from the electrical and ionic triggers of CPVT.

source.hint: Identify the specific mineral involved in cardiac cell excitability.
